summary: Set 133 Session 1 of 2, 'Say what shipped, and say it well' -- the release content for dabbler-ai-router 1.0.0 and extension 0.51.0. This session does not publish and does not tag; it makes the thing about to be tagged describe itself truthfully. SHIPPED (1) THE MISSING SET 125 ENTRY. The read-only tool grant landed in d13e7b9d and is NOT an ancestor of v0.34.0 (re-derived with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), so every seat on the published router has been dispatching routed calls under the old grant, and `grep -rl 'Set 125' changelog.d/` returned only the Set 120 S3 fragment that mentions it in passing. The new fragment files it under Security and states it as the consumer-visible security change it is: what a routed call could do before on the copilot-cli transport (arbitrary powershell, file create/edit, web fetch, sub-agent spawning against the LIVE working tree), what it can do now (view, grep, glob, from one shared _tool_grant_argv on BOTH dispatch paths), the matched-pair evidence (filesModified: ['sample.txt'] vs []), the 23 files modified with no human in the loop on 2026-08-12, and why it matters beyond the obvious -- a verifier able to edit the code it judges can fix a finding and report VERIFIED on its own edit. The api transport was never exposed (providers.py contains zero occurrences of 'tools'; verified, not assumed). SHIPPED (2) REAL VERSION SECTIONS. Folded 17 router + 13 extension fragments, then restructured both pending regions into the versions actually being tagged: one [1.0.0] and one [0.51.0], each carrying the earlier staged tranche beneath it as part of the SAME release (this repo's own 'folded into' precedent), rather than 17 loose [Unreleased] headings above a version. The transform touched heading lines only and asserted that every body line carried verbatim. SHIPPED (3) THE BREAKING CHANGE, SELF-REMEDYING. The 1.0.0 section now opens with the symptom a user actually sees (the literal LIGHTWEIGHT_REMOVED_MESSAGE), the one-line fix as a diff, and a working absolute link to the removal notice -- on one screen, before anything else. SHIPPED (4) THE MARKETPLACE LISTING. The extension README leads with what the framework IS and that the verification is checkable, uses the new media/ai-work-explorer.png by absolute raw.githubusercontent URL with alt text describing what the screenshot actually shows, and carries a 'Verification you can check' section of auditability claims plus an explicit block naming what is NOT claimed (no defect-catch rate, no 'catches bugs before they ship') and keeping the containment-not-a-sandbox register. Two FALSE statements removed: the $0-budget bullet offering 'or you skip verification with the decision logged' (no skip has existed since 1.0.0) and 'all three [keys] are required'. The 73%/32% savings headline was re-framed as what the shipped report actually computes -- a hypothetical Opus-only baseline -- rather than 'measured'. package.json's description and keywords were refreshed. SHIPPED (5) THE ROOT README'S TWO FALSE STATEMENTS. The tree is the AI Work Explorer (Set 132 S1), and Prerequisites no longer demands API-key accounts for all three providers -- it states the two answers, DIRECT_API with two of three as the working minimum or a keyless COPILOT_CLI seat, reconciled with the seat path described earlier in the same file. VERIFICATION: VERIFIED at round 4; gpt-5-6-sol every round, anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider by model-registry lookup. R1 discovery (2-way fan-out) returned ONE Major and it was right: the listing promised an unconditional cross-provider block while the same release documents an accepted same-provider fallback. Confirmed against the code rather than the prose -- route() lifts the exclusion when DirectApiPrecondition.degraded, for session-verification only, on DIRECT_API only. R2 supplementary (run BEFORE any remediation, per loop discipline) VERIFIED with 0 new. R3 REJECTED the first fix, correctly on two counts: package.json had been RE-WORDED ('independent verification built into every close') rather than fixed, which is the same unconditional claim on the Marketplace SEARCH surface, and the changelog argued that a labelled weaker verdict 'is not a substituted one' instead of reporting what happens. R4 VERIFIED, fix accepted, 0 findings. All four surfaces now state one contract: normally cross-provider, with the one configuration that is not named, scoped and machine-labelled (verification_qualification: same-provider). NOTE FOR STEP 9: the spec's own supported-claims list carries the absolute phrasing the verifier struck down; the copy follows the code, and the spec should be corrected rather than inherited. THREE DEFECTS FOUND BY DOING THE WORK, all fixed test-only, no product code (the spec's Non-goal). (a) `fold` emptied both corpora and turned 15 tests red: the falsifier battery in test_changelog_partition.py plants defects into the LIVE corpus, so it went red at exactly the moment a release is cut. The sandbox fixture now re-seeds from real released prose when the live corpus is folded, and the non-empty guard accepts the foldedAt contract check() already ships. (b) The same class at a SIBLING site the first pass missed -- test_drift_guard.py's reorder falsifier -- caught by the full pytest run and fixed the same way (G-008: a bug is a bug CLASS). (c) The single mocha failure was NOT a product bug: fileSystem test's landProjection helper, standing in for the Python writer, used Dirent.isFile() and so reproduced inside the stand-in writer the exact defect digestSetDirectory documents itself for avoiding; production code was already correct. Proven pre-existing by re-running it with this session's extension files stashed. It only EXECUTES on a Windows shell privileged enough to create a symlink and self-skips elsewhere, which is why it was not already known-red. OPEN DEFECT, PINNED NOT FIXED (operator ruling 2026-08-15, journaled): changelog.check() returns [] from its empty-corpus branch as soon as foldedAt is stamped, without ever comparing the originalSha256 that fold recorded for the whole document -- so between a release and the next contribution the round-trip guard verifies NOTHING and an edit to released history passes silently. The fix is ~6 lines and symmetric with the comparison the non-empty path already makes; it was deliberately not applied because this set forbids product code changes in a release commit. It is pinned by a strict-xfail falsifier that turns green the day it is closed, and it EARNED ITSELF TWICE during this session: the rewritten assertion caught post-restamp drift in both changelogs that `changelog check` reported as 'round trip OK' on the same tree. TEST COMPOSITION, stated rather than presented as one clean run: pytest 4664 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed in 213s, run at -n 8 rather than the declared -n auto per the operator's 2026-08-10 cap (identical specs and assertions; route journaled per G-004). mocha 1458 passing / 0 failing in 17s. playwright 32 passed / 0 failed in 2.9m via the declared command, 4 workers. Every suite ran AFTER the last change; the mocha run was re-taken because its covers includes ai_router/ and the sibling test fix staled the first green one. The post-verification changes are test-only, which under A4 owes no re-review. RESIDUALS with named owners: (1) the check() post-fold gap above; (2) 'Session Set Explorer' survives in 25 other markdown files (most are dated proposals; the live ones are close-out.md, copilot-seat-setup-checklist.md, repository-reference.md, session-state-schema.md, spec-md-schema.md) -- out of scope by the spec's Non-goals, not an oversight; (3) the corpus-seeding helper is now duplicated across two test modules and wants one shared home; (4) the Step 3.5 routed analyst again emitted model ids this router cannot call, which is the third set running. THE OPERATOR TAGS, NOT THIS SESSION: close, push, wait for CI green on the tagged commit, then push v1.0.0 and vsix-v0.51.0. Routed cost this session: $2.5583 across 6 calls. CORRECTION ON THE RECORD: this session first diagnosed the Layer 3 failure as ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE/VSCODE_* pollution from the orchestrator VS Code-hosted shell, and that was WRONG -- stripping those variables did not fix it. The cause is a stuck VS Code installer holding the vscode-updating mutex; the timing (~34.3s = 30s mutex wait + overhead, identical across all 32 specs) and the checkInnoSetupMutex log line are the evidence. The operator caught it from the outside by observing that no window ever appeared. Both the wrong turn and the correction are in decisions.jsonl, superseded rather than rewritten. Two probe errors are recorded with it: liveness was checked instead of window existence, and the check happened at 20s -- inside the 30s wait. LAYER 3 RESOLVED: the 32/32 launch failures were a stuck VS Code installer holding the machine-wide vscode-updating Inno Setup mutex since 04:36 -- every launched Code.exe waited 30s and died without creating a window, which is why every spec failed at ~34.3s regardless of version, worker count, shell or environment. The operator applied the pending update (VS Code 1.133.0) and the identical command passed 32/32 in 2.9m with NOTHING in the harness or the change set changed to make it pass. The aborted record stays on the ledger, superseded rather than rewritten. An earlier diagnosis blaming ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE/VSCODE_* shell pollution was WRONG and is withdrawn in decisions.jsonl; the operator caught it by observing that no window ever appeared, and the orchestrator had checked process liveness at 20s -- inside the 30s wait. OWED FOLLOW-ON (operator asked for it): a PR making the launch helper detect a held vscode-updating mutex and fail with that reason instead of 32 identical browser-has-been-closed timeouts, to land after this close and before the tag; scripts/ and src/ are both in .vscodeignore so it ships in neither artifact. CLOSE BACKSTOP (round 5) and its ADJUDICATION: the close ran a delta-scoped remediation-review of the two .baseline.json digest re-stamps and returned one Major -- the claimed Marketplace and changelog correction is absent from the fix delta -- which the operator adjudicated a FALSE POSITIVE on 2026-08-15 with deterministic falsifying evidence, and the session closed with --manual-verify carrying that record. It is a delta-scoping artifact: the round baselines on the round-4 COMPLETION anchor 9e4871a6a318, which already contains the corrections, so the delta legitimately has no hunk for package.json or ai_router/CHANGELOG.md and the verifier inferred absent-from-delta = absent-from-code. git show HEAD on both paths settles it -- the description reads normally cross-provider with no unconditional independence claim, and the 1.0.0 section carries the block headed It is not cross-provider in every case, and this release does not claim it is. Round 4 had already accepted these exact edits (1 accepted, 0 rejected). The round-5 artifacts are committed UNEDITED and the finding stands on the ledger beside its adjudication. The close is journaled as a verification REDUCTION (authority human, attested), because --manual-verify substitutes an attestation for the machine-settled evidence chain whatever the substance behind it. TWO MORE RESIDUALS from that round: post_round_delta calls the two .baseline.json paths not under any declared test surface while run_of_record affected lists both as pytest inputs -- the classifiers disagree about the same paths; and a delta-scoped review is handed whole-session claims with a delta-only bundle, with nothing telling it that a claim satisfied before the baseline is absent from the diff by construction.
